business_glossary_term: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) Reportable Indicator
description: Indicates whether this hold affects data elements that must be reported to IPEDS (True/False), such as holds that prevent graduation or enrollment.
reference: IPEDS Data Collection System, U.S. Department of Education

description: Username or identifier of the staff member or system process that last modified the hold record.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the hold record, supporting audit trail and data lineage.
Date on which the notification was sent to the student. Null if no notification was sent.
Method by which the student was notified of the hold (email, mail, portal, phone, sms, none).
Indicates whether a notification was sent to the student informing them of the hold (True/False).
Name or code of the institutional office or department that placed the hold (e.g., Bursar, Registrar, Student Health, Library, Parking Services, Dean of Students).
Indicates whether authorized staff are permitted to override this hold to allow restricted services (True/False).
Role or position authorized to override this hold (e.g., Registrar, Dean, Bursar, Department Chair). Null if override is not allowed.
Username or identifier of the staff member or system process that placed the hold.
Date on which the hold was placed on the student record.
Numeric priority level of the hold, used to determine processing order when multiple holds exist. Lower numbers typically indicate higher priority.

Detailed textual description of the reason the hold was placed, providing context for the restriction (e.g., outstanding tuition balance, missing immunization records, academic probation, library fines).
Indicates whether this hold blocks the student from registering for courses (True/False).
Textual description of the reason the hold was released (e.g., payment received, documentation submitted, appeal approved, administrative override).
Username or identifier of the staff member or system process that released the hold. Null if the hold is still active.
Date on which the hold was manually released or cleared. Null if the hold is still active.
Indicates whether the hold was automatically generated by a system process (True) or manually placed by staff (False).
Academic term code associated with the hold, if the hold is term-specific (e.g., 202401 for Spring 2024). Null if the hold is not term-specific.
Indicates whether this hold blocks the release of official transcripts (True/False).
Unique identifier for the leave of absence record. Primary key for the leave_of_absence product.
Unique identifier of the faculty or staff member who approved the leave of absence. Links to employee or faculty record.

Foreign key linking to enrollment.term. Business justification: Leave of absence administration requires formal term linkage for leave start dates to calculate return eligibility, financial aid impact, and degree timeline adjustments. Current leave_start_term is a
Unique identifier of the student taking the leave of absence. Links to the student master record.

Student's academic standing status at the time the leave of absence began. Good standing indicates satisfactory academic performance, academic probation indicates below-standard performance with conditions, academic suspension indicates temporary removal from enrollment, academic dismissal indicates permanent removal.
Actual date when the student returned from leave and re-enrolled. Null if student has not yet returned. Used to measure leave duration accuracy and Title IV compliance.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations; Ellucian Banner Student Information System

description: Indicates whether the student's academic advisor was notified of the leave of absence. True if advisor notified, false otherwise. Important for continuity of advising relationship.
Date on which the leave of absence request was officially approved by the approving authority. Null if not yet approved or if denied.
Name or title of the institutional official who approved the leave of absence request (e.g., Dean of Students, Registrar, Academic Advisor).
Additional administrative notes or comments about the leave of absence, including special circumstances, follow-up actions, or coordination with other offices.
Timestamp when this leave of absence record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance tracking.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; FERPA

description: Total number of credit hours the student had successfully completed at the time the leave of absence began. Used for degree progress tracking and SAP calculations.
Number of days by which the leave of absence extends the student's expected degree completion timeline. Used for academic planning and advising.
Indicates whether an enrollment hold is placed on the student's record during the leave period, preventing registration until return conditions are met. True if hold is active, false otherwise.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; Institutional Policy

description: Anticipated date when the student plans to return from leave and re-enroll. Used for planning and Title IV compliance tracking.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations

description: Academic term code when the student is expected to return from leave and resume enrollment. Follows institutional term coding convention.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; IPEDS

description: Indicates whether the leave of absence affects the student's financial aid eligibility, Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) status, or Title IV aid clock. True if financial aid is impacted, false otherwise.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations; SAP (Satisfactory Academic Progress) Policy

description: Student's cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) at the time the leave of absence began. Used to track academic standing and eligibility for return. Expressed on a 4.0 scale.

Status of the student's on-campus housing contract during the leave period. Active indicates contract remains in force, suspended indicates temporary pause, terminated indicates contract ended, not_applicable indicates student had no housing contract.

business_glossary_term: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) Reportable Flag
description: Indicates whether this leave of absence must be reported in IPEDS enrollment and retention surveys. True if reportable, false otherwise. Depends on leave duration and timing relative to census dates.
reference: IPEDS (Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System); U.S. Department of Education

description: Timestamp when this leave of absence record was most recently updated. Audit field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; FERPA

description: Official end date of the approved leave of absence period. Represents the last day the student is on leave status before expected return.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations

description: Effective date when the leave of absence officially begins. Marks the first day the student is no longer enrolled.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations; FERPA

description: Current status of the leave of absence request in its lifecycle. Pending indicates awaiting approval, approved indicates authorization granted, denied indicates request rejected, active indicates student is currently on leave, returned indicates student has resumed enrollment, withdrawn indicates student withdrew the request.

Category of leave of absence granted to the student. Medical covers health-related absences, personal covers non-medical personal reasons, military covers active duty service, parental covers childbirth or adoption, research covers off-campus research opportunities, and academic covers study abroad or exchange programs.
reference: FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act); Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations

description: Status of the student's meal plan during the leave period. Active indicates plan continues, suspended indicates temporary pause, terminated indicates plan ended, not_applicable indicates student had no meal plan.
Username or identifier of the system user who last modified this leave of absence record. Audit field for accountability and compliance.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; FERPA

description: Indicates whether the student has confirmed their intent to re-enroll after the leave period. True if re-enrollment confirmed, false if not confirmed or student withdrew permanently.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; Institutional Policy

description: Actual academic term code when the student re-enrolled after returning from leave. May differ from expected_return_term if student delayed return. Null if student has not yet re-enrolled.
reference: Ellucian Banner Student Information System; IPEDS

description: Detailed narrative explanation provided by the student for requesting the leave of absence. May contain sensitive personal information. Classified as confidential to protect student privacy.
reference: FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act)

description: Date on which the student submitted the leave of absence request. Represents the business event timestamp for the leave request initiation.
Specific conditions or requirements the student must meet before being permitted to return from leave (e.g., medical clearance, academic advising meeting, financial holds resolved).
reference: Institutional Policy; Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations

business_glossary_term: Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) Clock Stopped Flag
description: Indicates whether the Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) maximum timeframe clock is stopped during this leave period. True if SAP clock is paused, false if it continues to run. Critical for Title IV financial aid compliance.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations; SAP Policy

description: Indicates whether supporting documentation (medical records, military orders, etc.) was submitted with the leave request. True if documentation provided, false otherwise.

Indicates whether the leave of absence meets Title IV federal financial aid compliance requirements (duration limits, approval documentation, return expectations). True if compliant, false if non-compliant.
reference: Title IV Federal Student Aid Regulations; U.S. Department of Education

description: Indicates whether the student is eligible for a tuition refund based on the timing of the leave relative to the institutional refund schedule. True if eligible for refund, false otherwise.
reference: Institutional Refund Policy; Student Accounts Policy

description: Percentage of tuition eligible for refund based on the leave start date and institutional refund schedule. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 75.00 for 75% refund).
reference: Institutional Refund Policy; Student Accounts Policy

business_glossary_term: Student Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) Evaluation ID
description: Unique identifier for each formal SAP evaluation record. Primary key for the student SAP evaluation entity.

Foreign key linking to enrollment.term. Business justification: Title IV satisfactory academic progress evaluations occur at term end for financial aid eligibility determination. Evaluation_term_code insufficient for automated SAP evaluation scheduling tied to ter
User ID of the system user who created this SAP evaluation record. Part of audit trail for compliance and accountability.
User ID of the system user who last modified this SAP evaluation record. Part of audit trail for compliance and accountability.
Unique identifier of the financial aid counselor or staff member who conducted this SAP evaluation. Links to staff/employee master record.
Unique identifier of the student being evaluated for Satisfactory Academic Progress. Links to the student master record.
Indicates whether a formal academic plan document has been attached to this SAP evaluation record. True if plan is on file.
Indicates whether an academic plan is required as a condition of the SAP appeal approval or probation status. True if academic plan is mandatory.
URL or file path to the stored academic plan document outlining the student's path to return to satisfactory academic progress. Null if no plan exists.
Academic year for which this SAP evaluation applies (e.g., 2023-2024). Used for multi-year SAP tracking and IPEDS reporting.
Date on which Title IV financial aid was reinstated following successful SAP appeal or academic plan completion. Null if aid was not reinstated.
Date on which Title IV financial aid was suspended due to SAP failure. Null if aid was not suspended.

Decision outcome of the SAP appeal: approved (appeal granted, aid continues under academic plan), denied (appeal rejected, aid remains suspended), pending (under review), or withdrawn (student withdrew appeal).
Date on which the SAP appeal decision was rendered. Null if appeal is pending or no appeal was submitted.
Primary reason cited by the student for the SAP appeal (e.g., medical emergency, family crisis, death of relative, military deployment). Free-text field capturing mitigating circumstances.
Date on which the student submitted their SAP appeal. Null if no appeal was submitted.
Indicates whether the student submitted a formal SAP appeal following suspension or warning. True if appeal was submitted.
Free-text comments or notes from the evaluating counselor regarding this SAP evaluation, including special circumstances, exceptions, or additional context.
Percentage of attempted credits that the student has successfully completed (credits_earned / credits_attempted * 100). Represents the quantitative measure (pace) of SAP.
Minimum completion rate (pace) percentage required for satisfactory academic progress. Federal regulations typically require at least 67% completion rate.
Timestamp when this SAP evaluation record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for compliance and data lineage.
Total cumulative credit hours attempted by the student at the time of this SAP evaluation. Includes all enrolled credits regardless of completion or grade outcome.
Total cumulative credit hours successfully completed (earned) by the student at the time of this SAP evaluation. Used to calculate pace/completion rate.
Student's cumulative GPA at the time of this SAP evaluation. Used to assess qualitative measure of academic progress against institutional minimum GPA threshold.
The date on which this SAP evaluation was formally conducted and recorded. Critical for Title IV compliance audit trails.

Type of SAP evaluation conducted: annual (end-of-year standard review), mid-year (mid-term checkpoint), appeal (student-initiated review following suspension), reinstatement (review after academic plan completion), probation_review (review during probation period), or warning_review (review during warning period).

Current Title IV financial aid eligibility status resulting from this SAP evaluation: eligible (aid continues), suspended (aid stopped), reinstated (aid resumed after appeal), or conditional (aid continues under academic plan).
Indicates whether the student met the minimum cumulative GPA requirement for SAP at the time of evaluation. True if cumulative_gpa >= gpa_threshold.
Minimum cumulative GPA required for satisfactory academic progress at the time of this evaluation. Threshold may vary by student level (undergraduate, graduate) and program.

business_glossary_term: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) Reportable Flag
description: Indicates whether this SAP evaluation record should be included in IPEDS reporting submissions. True if reportable.
Indicates whether this SAP evaluation record is currently active and represents the most recent evaluation for the student in the given term. True if active, false if superseded or voided.
Timestamp when this SAP evaluation record was last modified. Critical for tracking changes to SAP status and appeal decisions.
Maximum number of credit hours allowed for the student to complete their program (typically 150% of published program length). Once exceeded, student loses Title IV eligibility.

Indicates whether the student is within the maximum timeframe allowed to complete their program. True if credits_attempted < maximum_timeframe_credits and student can mathematically complete within maximum timeframe.
Date on which the student was notified of their SAP evaluation results. Critical for compliance documentation.
Method by which the student was notified of SAP results: email, mail (postal), portal (student information system), or in_person (face-to-face meeting).
Indicates whether the student was formally notified of their SAP evaluation results. True if notification was sent.

Overall SAP status determination: satisfactory (all requirements met), warning (first failure, aid continues), probation (appeal approved with academic plan, aid continues), suspension (aid suspended), or reinstatement (aid reinstated after successful appeal or plan completion).
Indicates whether the student met the minimum completion rate (pace) requirement for SAP. True if completion_rate >= completion_rate_threshold.
Name of the source system from which this SAP evaluation record originated (e.g., Ellucian Banner Financial Aid module). Used for data lineage and integration tracking.
Unique identifier for the visa and immigration record. Primary key for the visa_immigration product.

Foreign key linking to research.export_control_review. Business justification: Export control reviews must document foreign national students with access to controlled technology or data; regulatory requirement under EAR/ITAR for universities conducting defense or dual-use resea
Unique identifier of the international student associated with this visa and immigration record. Links to the student master record in the Student Information System (SIS).

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_requirement. Business justification: SEVIS reporting is a federal regulatory requirement under SEVP. Immigration status tracking directly supports compliance with F-1/J-1 visa regulations. Essential for SEVIS batch reporting and complian

The date until which the student is authorized to remain in the United States. For F-1 and J-1 students, this is typically D/S (Duration of Status) which extends through the program end date plus any grace period.
reference: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Form I-94

description: The three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the student's country of birth. Required for SEVIS reporting and visa applications.
The three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the student's country of citizenship. This is the country that issued the student's passport.

business_glossary_term: Curricular Practical Training (CPT) Authorization End Date
description: The end date of the Curricular Practical Training (CPT) period. Students must cease CPT employment by this date unless a new authorization is granted.

business_glossary_term: Curricular Practical Training (CPT) Authorization Start Date
description: The start date of the Curricular Practical Training (CPT) period for F-1 students. CPT allows students to engage in internships or employment that is an integral part of their curriculum while enrolled.

Indicates whether the CPT authorization is for part-time employment (20 hours or less per week) or full-time employment (more than 20 hours per week). Full-time CPT for 12 months or more makes students ineligible for post-completion OPT.
The timestamp when this visa and immigration record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

The program end date listed on the Form DS-2019, indicating when the exchange visitor is expected to complete their program. J-1 visitors must complete their program by this date or request an extension.
reference: U.S. Department of State, Form DS-2019

description: The date on which the Certificate of Eligibility for Exchange Visitor Status (Form DS-2019) was issued to the J-1 exchange visitor by the institution's Responsible Officer (RO). Required for J-1 visa holders.
reference: U.S. Department of State, Form DS-2019

description: The email address of the Designated School Official (DSO) responsible for this student's SEVIS record. Used for official communications regarding the student's immigration status.

The name of the Designated School Official (DSO) who is the primary point of contact for this student's SEVIS record. The DSO is responsible for maintaining the student's record and ensuring compliance with SEVP regulations.
The date on which the Employment Authorization Document (EAD) expires. Students must cease employment or renew their EAD before this date.
The date on which the Employment Authorization Document (EAD) was issued by USCIS.

The unique number on the Employment Authorization Document (EAD card, Form I-766) issued by USCIS. This card authorizes the student to work in the United States during OPT or other authorized employment periods.
The date on which the student most recently entered the United States. This date is recorded on the Form I-94 Arrival/Departure Record and is critical for calculating authorized stay periods.
reference: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Form I-94

business_glossary_term: Full Course of Study Compliance Flag
description: Boolean flag indicating whether the student is currently enrolled in a full course of study as required by their visa status. F-1 students must be enrolled full-time (typically 12 credit hours for undergraduates, 9 for graduates) to maintain status.

The date on which the student's grace period ends. F-1 students receive a 60-day grace period after program completion or OPT end date. J-1 students receive a 30-day grace period. Students must depart the U.S. or change status by this date.
The program end date listed on the Form I-20, indicating when the student is expected to complete their academic program. Students must complete their program by this date or request an extension.

The date on which the Certificate of Eligibility for Nonimmigrant Student Status (Form I-20) was issued to the F or M student by the institution's Designated School Official (DSO). Required for F-1 and M-1 visa holders.

The unique 11-digit admission number from the Form I-94 Arrival/Departure Record issued by U.S. Customs and Border Protection upon entry to the United States. This number is used to verify lawful admission and authorized stay.
reference: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Form I-94

description: The timestamp of the most recent update to the student's SEVIS record. SEVIS records must be updated within 21 days of any change in student status, program, or personal information.

The date by which the next mandatory SEVIS report is due. Schools must report certain events (enrollment verification, program completion, status changes) within specific timeframes to maintain SEVP certification.
Boolean flag indicating whether the student is authorized to work off campus through CPT, OPT, severe economic hardship authorization, or other special circumstances.

Boolean flag indicating whether the student is authorized to work on campus. F-1 students are generally authorized to work on campus up to 20 hours per week while school is in session and full-time during breaks.

business_glossary_term: Optional Practical Training (OPT) Authorization End Date
description: The end date of the Optional Practical Training (OPT) period. Students must cease employment and depart the U.S. or change status by this date unless they have applied for a STEM extension or other status change.

business_glossary_term: Optional Practical Training (OPT) Authorization Start Date
description: The start date of the Optional Practical Training (OPT) period for F-1 students. OPT allows students to work in their field of study for up to 12 months (or 24 months for STEM extension) after completing their academic program.

The type of OPT authorization. Pre-completion OPT allows students to work part-time while enrolled. Post-completion OPT allows full-time work after graduation. STEM extension provides an additional 24 months for STEM degree holders.
The expiration date of the student's passport. Students must maintain a valid passport (typically valid for at least 6 months into the future) to maintain legal status in the United States.
The passport number from the student's valid passport. This field should be encrypted at rest to protect sensitive personal information. Required for SEVIS reporting and visa tracking.

The U.S. port of entry (airport, seaport, or land border crossing) through which the student most recently entered the United States. Examples include JFK (New York), LAX (Los Angeles), or ATL (Atlanta).

Boolean flag indicating whether the student has been authorized by the Designated School Official (DSO) to take a reduced course load due to academic difficulties, medical reasons, or initial difficulty with English language or reading requirements.
